_meta.notes: Hosted on the real Astronaut Complex because the claim being tested is a division of labour across the whole panel: the roster rows above state WHERE each kerbal is and carry no controls at all, and the two ways off a course sit once, together, on the course itself. Ludrey and Nedcas share one course, which is the only shape where RP-1's two ways out are genuinely different acts: cancelling ends it for both, removing takes one of them off and leaves it running. Drawn on the rows instead, that single course rendered its name, its progress, its finish date and its cancel button twice
_meta.why-a-removal-per-student: The subject is what decides where a control lives. Cancelling is about the COURSE, so there is one of it; removing is about one named student, so there is one per student, and both are on the thing they act on rather than scattered across the roster
_meta.why-the-stand-in-host: Rendered in the stand-in host rather than on the real Astronaut Complex, and that is the harness telling the truth about the app: the courses live behind a TAB, a tab's content is not mounted until it is selected, and the scene driver's presses run after the fixture has emitted. Nothing would have subscribed. In a running app the stream replays the last value on subscribe, so the tab fills the moment it is opened; here the picture is of the tab's content on its own. The panel with the tab strip is the sibling crew-schedule-three-states scene
